samples.summary: The `loadSpillBlockers()` calls added to `undo()`/`redo()` have no test — the "reload" test is a hand-rolled proxy that never invokes undo or redo
samples.evidence: The diff's stated motivation is that undo/redo replace cell data without recalculating, so the blocker map must be rebuilt (sheet.ts undo ~line 5096, redo ~line 5135). The only test offered is calculation.test.ts:406 'a reload derives the blocker map…', which constructs `new Sheet(store)` and calls `reloaded.loadSpillBlockers()` directly (line 420-421), explicitly saying it 'stands in for undo/redo'. Grepping the whole sheets test tree for `.undo(`/`.redo(` returns no files, so deleting both new `await this.loadSpillBlockers()` lines from `undo()` and `redo()` would leave every test green. The regression the change fixes (permanent `#REF!` after undo) is therefore uncovered.
searchedFor: Grep 'loadSpillBlockers' repo-wide → only src + calculation.test.ts + worksheet.ts

samples.summary: `Worksheet.initialize` wiring (bindRefusalNotices + loadSpillBlockers) is untested; the notice test bypasses initialize by calling prototype methods on a synthetic `this`
samples.evidence: worksheet-notice.test.ts `wire()` (lines 22-28) does `setOnNotice.call(ctx, …)` and `bindRefusalNotices.call(ctx, sheet)` on a bare object literal, deliberately replicating what initialize does rather than running it (the src comment at worksheet.ts admits it is 'Kept out of `initialize` so the refusal-to-message path can be exercised without booting a whole grid'). Nothing calls `Worksheet.initialize` in any test (grep 'initialize(' in packages/sheets/test → no matches), so both new lines inside initialize — `this.bindRefusalNotices(sheet)` and `await this.sheet.loadSpillBlockers()` — could be deleted with the suite still green, and the user-visible toast path plus the document-open blocker rebuild would silently stop working. The tests prove `refusalMessage` mapping only, not that the view ever subscribes.

samples.summary: The copy-paste (non-cut) branch that materializes spill ghosts into static cells has no test
samples.evidence: In `paste`, the new loop (diff hunk around sheet.ts:2329-2341) has two outcomes: cut-with-anchor → `grid.delete(sref)` (covered by calculation.test.ts:385 'cut-pasting a spill re-creates its ghosts instead of copying them'), and everything else → `const materialized = {...cell}; delete materialized.spillAnchor; grid.set(...)`. No test performs a plain copy of a spill range and pastes it, nor a cut of ghosts whose anchor is outside the copied selection. Grep for 'spill'/'MUNIT'/'spillAnchor' in packages/sheets/test/sheet/clipboard.test.ts returns nothing, and calculation.test.ts contains only the cut variant. So the materialization rule (pasted ghosts become static values that later block the anchor's re-spill) is asserted nowhere.
searchedFor: Grep 'paste\(|copy\(' in packages/sheets/test → clipboard.test.ts, pivot-protection.test.ts, calculation.test.ts

samples.summary: 'hands Spreadsheet.onNotice through to the worksheet' only asserts a mock was called on a fabricated `this` — it cannot fail if real wiring breaks
samples.evidence: Lines 130-140 build `{ worksheet: { setOnNotice: vi.fn() } }`, call `Spreadsheet.prototype.onNotice.call(...)`, and assert `setOnNotice` was called with the callback. The real `Worksheet` is mocked away and no `Spreadsheet` is constructed, so the test restates the one-line body of `onNotice` and would still pass if `Worksheet.setOnNotice` stopped storing the callback or if `Spreadsheet` never held a worksheet at that point. It is delegation-shaped mock-only coverage, not behavior coverage.

samples.summary: 'stays silent until a host registers a notice callback' asserts something that holds regardless of the feature
samples.evidence: Lines 119-127 assert `sheet.moveRangeTo(...)` `resolves.toBeUndefined()`. `moveRangeTo` returns `Promise<void>` on both the refusal path and the success path, so `toBeUndefined()` is true whatever happens; the test's only real content is 'does not throw' via the `this.onNoticeCallback?.()` optional chain. It never asserts that no message was produced (there is no collector wired), so it reads as coverage of the unregistered-host case while asserting nothing specific to it.

samples.summary: 'reports nothing when there is no fill range to apply' never reaches the refusal code it appears to guard
samples.evidence: The test autofills A1 onto A1, which `autofill` rejects before the merge check that calls `this.refuse('merge-autofill')`, so `expect(refusals).toEqual([])` would pass even if the refusal call were unconditional at the merge branch. Harmless, but it does not add signal beyond the existing empty-fill test above it.

samples.summary: The frontend `s.onNotice(...) → toast.error` wiring has no test in packages/frontend
samples.evidence: The new subscription in sheet-view.tsx (diff hunk at ~line 1018) is the only place the refusal message reaches a user. packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet contains only image-downscale, csv-actions, csv-doc-size and image-upload tests (glob '*.test.*'), none touching sheet-view; grep for 'onNotice' in packages/frontend/src matches sheet-view.tsx alone. Given frontend also has no `tsc` lane, a broken or removed subscription would be caught by nothing.

finding.summary: The `loadSpillBlockers()` calls added to `undo()`/`redo()` have no test — the "reload" test is a hand-rolled proxy that never invokes undo or redo
finding.evidence: The diff's stated motivation is that undo/redo replace cell data without recalculating, so the blocker map must be rebuilt (sheet.ts undo ~line 5096, redo ~line 5135). The only test offered is calculation.test.ts:406 'a reload derives the blocker map…', which constructs `new Sheet(store)` and calls `reloaded.loadSpillBlockers()` directly (line 420-421), explicitly saying it 'stands in for undo/redo'. Grepping the whole sheets test tree for `.undo(`/`.redo(` returns no files, so deleting both new `await this.loadSpillBlockers()` lines from `undo()` and `redo()` would leave every test green. The regression the change fixes (permanent `#REF!` after undo) is therefore uncovered.
searchedFor: Grep 'loadSpillBlockers' repo-wide → only src + calculation.test.ts + worksheet.ts

verdict.reason: The absence claim checks out. sheet.ts:5103 and :5140 add `await this.loadSpillBlockers()` inside undo()/redo(), but no test anywhere in the repo invokes Sheet.undo()/redo(): a repo-wide grep for `\.undo\(|\.redo\(` across all test/spec files matches notes, docs, slides, design-editor and frontend stores but zero sheets test files; a case-insensitive `undo|redo|history` sweep of packages/sheets/test yields only the comment at calculation.test.ts:417. Indirect routes are also uncovered — the only callers are the Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y handlers at src/view/worksheet.ts:5087,5101, and the sheets view tests (test/view/keymap.test.ts:46 only tests matchesKeyCombo; worksheet-keymap.test.ts has no undo) never reach them; nor do the frontend spreadsheet tests or cli sheets tests. The sole offered test (calculation.test.ts:406-429) builds a second `new Sheet(store)` and calls loadSpillBlockers() directly at line 421, self-describing as a stand-in for undo/redo. Reinforcing this: MemStore.undo()/redo() return {success:false} (src/store/memory.ts:555-561), so the whole reload block in undo()/redo() is unreachable with the store every sheets test uses — deleting both new lines leaves the suite green, and the undo-specific regression (permanent #REF! after undo) has no guard. The underlying rebuild mechanism is tested, which is a mitigating factor, but the changed behavior at the call sites has no test at all, so the finding is real and in-lane (missing test for a changed behavior).

finding.summary: `Worksheet.initialize` wiring (bindRefusalNotices + loadSpillBlockers) is untested; the notice test bypasses initialize by calling prototype methods on a synthetic `this`
finding.evidence: worksheet-notice.test.ts `wire()` (lines 22-28) does `setOnNotice.call(ctx, …)` and `bindRefusalNotices.call(ctx, sheet)` on a bare object literal, deliberately replicating what initialize does rather than running it (the src comment at worksheet.ts admits it is 'Kept out of `initialize` so the refusal-to-message path can be exercised without booting a whole grid'). Nothing calls `Worksheet.initialize` in any test (grep 'initialize(' in packages/sheets/test → no matches), so both new lines inside initialize — `this.bindRefusalNotices(sheet)` and `await this.sheet.loadSpillBlockers()` — could be deleted with the suite still green, and the user-visible toast path plus the document-open blocker rebuild would silently stop working. The tests prove `refusalMessage` mapping only, not that the view ever subscribes.

verdict.reason:
The factual core of the finding checks out: no test anywhere boots `Worksheet.initialize`. I grepped all of packages/sheets for `.initialize(` and the only hits are src call sites (`packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:96` -> `worksheet.initialize`, `worksheet.ts:436`); the frontend tests that do reference the sheets entry point mock it away (`packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/lakehouse-view.test.tsx:52-57,141` mock `initialize` from '@wafflebase/sheets'), and there is no e2e/playwright suite (no `**/e2e/**` files) exercising the harness pages that call it. So the two lines inside `initialize` (worksheet.ts:417, :424) are indeed uncovered as call sites.

But under this lens's rubric that is a minor breadth gap, not a blocking one, because both underlying behaviors DO have real, non-vacuous tests, and the rubric says not to flag "add more tests" unless a behavior change "genuinely lacks any meaningful test":
1. Refusal -> toast: `packages/sheets/test/view/worksheet-notice.test.ts` is not fake coverage. It drives a REAL `Sheet` over a real `MemStore` through `mergeSelection`/`moveRangeTo`/`autofill` and asserts the exact host-visible strings, plus a negative case (line 92-108, no message when the gesture succeeds) and a no-callback-registered case (110-128). The only thing stubbed is the DOM-heavy `Worksheet` instance itself (the src comment at worksheet.ts:861-864 documents that split); `bindRefusalNotices`, `refusalMessage`, `setOnRefusal` and the model refusal path are all real, so the test fails if the mapping or the subscription logic breaks.
2. Document-open blocker rebuild: `packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts:406-429` ("a reload derives the blocker map so a cleared blocker still frees the anchor") constructs a second `Sheet` over the same store, explicitly standing in for "opening the document", calls `loadSpillBlockers()`, and asserts the `#REF!` clears — i.e. the semantics the initialize line exists to trigger are covered.

What remains untested is a two-line wiring call inside a method that requires booting a canvas grid; that is "coverage could be broader" (minor), not a vacuous test presented as coverage nor a behavior shipped with no meaningful test. The one mock-only assertion in the file (line 130-140, `Spreadsheet.onNotice` delegates to `worksheet.setOnNotice`) is a trivial one-line delegation, at most a nit.

finding.summary: The copy-paste (non-cut) branch that materializes spill ghosts into static cells has no test
finding.evidence: In `paste`, the new loop (diff hunk around sheet.ts:2329-2341) has two outcomes: cut-with-anchor → `grid.delete(sref)` (covered by calculation.test.ts:385 'cut-pasting a spill re-creates its ghosts instead of copying them'), and everything else → `const materialized = {...cell}; delete materialized.spillAnchor; grid.set(...)`. No test performs a plain copy of a spill range and pastes it, nor a cut of ghosts whose anchor is outside the copied selection. Grep for 'spill'/'MUNIT'/'spillAnchor' in packages/sheets/test/sheet/clipboard.test.ts returns nothing, and calculation.test.ts contains only the cut variant. searchedFor: Grep 'paste\(|copy\(' in packages/sheets/test → clipboard.test.ts, pivot-protection.test.ts, calculation.test.ts

verdict.reason: The paste loop at sheet.ts:2327-2341 has two outcomes: cut-with-anchor deletes the ghost (covered by calculation.test.ts:385 'cut-pasting a spill re-creates its ghosts instead of copying them'), and every other case materializes the ghost into a static cell by stripping spillAnchor. I searched repo-wide for any test that could reach the materialization branch: all *.test.ts containing 'spill' (5 sheets files + 2 unrelated docs files), all test files using a spilling function (MUNIT|MINVERSE|MMULT|TRANSPOSE), all test files calling .copy(/.cut( (calculation.test.ts, clipboard.test.ts, two unrelated backend specs), and all *.integration/*.e2e/*.mjs/tsx files for spillAnchor/MUNIT (none). clipboard.test.ts has zero occurrences of ghost/Anchor/store.set. Within calculation.test.ts the only clipboard calls are lines 251-257 (cut carrying a blocker, not a ghost) and 385-404 (cut carrying the anchor) — both take the delete branch. Ghosts can only reach a copied grid via a spill formula or a direct store.set with spillAnchor, and both surfaces were grepped, so no counterexample exists. A plain copy-paste of a spill range, and a cut of ghosts whose anchor is outside the selection, are untested behaviors — major under the missing-tests rubric.
